issues.legal_issue: A will is proved when its execution, attestation, the testator’s testamentary capacity, and the testator’s free and informed choice are established by the required evidence.
material_facts: The will’s execution was not disputed, and an attesting witness testified about the will being read and signed and about the witnesses’ attestation.
The court found that the testator understood the will’s contents and acted of his free will.
The testator was unwell, but the court proceeded on the basis that illness did not itself establish a lack of mental capacity.
issues.conclusion: The court held that the will had been proved as a genuine, freely made testamentary disposition.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 63 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, an unprivileged will must be executed and attested in the prescribed manner; under Section 68 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, its execution must be proved by at least one available and capable attesting witness. The propounder must establish execution, testamentary capacity, and the testator’s free and informed choice. The court relied on Apoline D’Souza v. John D’Souza, B. Venkatamuni v. C.J. Ayodhya Ram Singh, Niranjan Umeshchandra Joshi v. Mrudula Jyoti Rao, and H. Venkatachala Iyengar v. B.N. Thimmajamma.

rule.if: will_validity_contested and testator_signature_proved and attesting_witness_examined and testator_understood_disposition and testator_had_testamentary_capacity and free_volition_established

predicates.will_validity_contested: A party challenged whether a will was validly made.
predicates.testator_signature_proved: Evidence established that the testator signed the will.
predicates.attesting_witness_examined: At least one attesting witness gave evidence about the will’s execution and attestation.
predicates.testator_understood_disposition: The evidence established that the testator understood the nature and effect of the disposition.
predicates.testator_had_testamentary_capacity: The evidence established that the testator had the mental capacity to make the disposition.
predicates.free_volition_established: The evidence established that the testator acted freely in making the will.

issues.definition: When a challenged will is supported by proof of the testator’s signature, the required witness evidence, capacity, understanding, and free choice, its execution is proved.

issues.legal_issue: Excluding or reducing the share of a natural heir does not, by itself, make a will suspicious; the circumstances surrounding the disposition must be considered as a whole.
material_facts: The will preferred the testator’s sister’s children and their children, who had cared for and supported him while he was ill and dependent on them.
The testator’s son had not cared for him or met his treatment expenses, and the will provided for a payment to the son.
The testator lived for seven years after making the registered will and did not cancel it.
The challengers also relied on the testator’s illness, the beneficiaries’ relationship to the will, the choice of witnesses, and the circumstances of execution.
issues.conclusion: The court found no suspicious circumstance that prevented acceptance of the will, and held that the exclusion of a natural heir alone was insufficient to invalidate it.
issues.legal_principle: The propounder must explain suspicious circumstances to the court’s satisfaction, but the exclusion of natural heirs or the grant of a lesser share to them is not, without more, suspicious. The court must assess the relevant background and circumstances rationally. It relied on H. Venkatachala Iyengar v. B.N. Thimmajamma, Ramabai Padmakar Patil v. Rukminibai Vishnu Vekhande, S. Sundaresa Pai v. Sumangala T. Pai, and Gurdial Kaur v. Kartar Kaur.

rule.if: will_validity_contested and natural_heir_excluded and beneficiaries_supported_testator and natural_heir_failed_to_care_for_testator

predicates.will_validity_contested: A party challenged whether a will was validly made.
predicates.natural_heir_excluded: The will excluded a natural heir or gave that heir less than the heir might otherwise receive.
predicates.beneficiaries_supported_testator: The beneficiaries had cared for or supported the testator.
predicates.natural_heir_failed_to_care_for_testator: The natural heir had not cared for or supported the testator.

issues.definition: When a challenged will excludes a natural heir but the beneficiaries supported the testator and the heir did not, the exclusion alone does not make the will suspicious.

issues.legal_issue: A challenger who alleges that a will was procured by coercion or undue influence bears the burden of proving that allegation.
material_facts: The challengers alleged that the testator’s signature had been obtained through undue influence or coercion.
The court found that the challengers had failed to prove the allegation.
issues.conclusion: The court held that the allegation of coercion or undue influence was not established.
issues.legal_principle: Where fraud, coercion, or undue influence is alleged against a will, the burden of proving that allegation rests on the challenger. The court relied on Niranjan Umeshchandra Joshi v. Mrudula Jyoti Rao, Madhukar D. Shende v. Tarabai Shedage, and Sridevi v. Jayaraja Shetty.

predicates.will_validity_contested: A party challenged whether a will was validly made.
predicates.challenger_alleged_coercion_or_undue_inf: The challenger asserted that coercion or undue influence affected the making of the will.
predicates.challenger_failed_to_prove_allegation: The challenger did not establish the alleged coercion or undue influence with evidence.

issues.definition: When a challenger alleges coercion or undue influence in a will challenge but fails to prove it, that allegation is not established.
